exposure: manual rotation for persistent occiput posterior position
cohort: 460 women with a singleton pregnancy after 37 weeks of gestation with a fetus in persistent occiput posterior position
finding: Successful manual rotation for persistent occiput posterior position is associated with decreased rates of occiput posterior position at delivery, operative delivery, and anal sphincter injuries.
mod_finding: Successful manual rotation was associated with a decrease in occiput posterior position at vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery, and operative vaginal delivery.
